recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No current FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-14341; a future legacy terminology-tooling refresh could consider tools/tx/v3/source_nl.xml as housekeeping outside this reconciliation.
issue_request: FHIR-14341 was a Published/Persuasive PA change request to replace the outdated term hermaphrodite with intersex in the v3 AdministrativeGender UN (Undifferentiated) definition without changing the meaning.
initial_application: No git commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-14341 was found. PA January 2019 WGM minutes record acceptance, and commit f04f624af84359656111d4bfbef5e06703525fef updated the historical v3 source to the 2019 vocabulary that contains intersex and intersekse-conditie wording. Commit 5c0494aacfd0b8bd52bc72c587aa89d0a64246f8 removed UTG content from core build scope, and commit 02557a9364dab7c1c03bc9597ec62955ee76e635 later carried the updated v3 source under tools/tx/v3/source.xml.
additional_context: Current core source composes AdministrativeGender from http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/v3-AdministrativeGender, and current THO JSON for code UN contains the approved intersex wording. Remaining hermaphrodite hits are in release-history snapshots, DICOM imported terminology, spelling dictionaries, or an old separate Dutch helper file not referenced by source/fhir.ini. FHIR-16340, already represented on the combined branch, bounds this issue by confirming that Intersex was not added as a separate AdministrativeGender code.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current active/current authoritative surfaces already match the Jira request, and editing stale historical or auxiliary files would not correct the current FHIR specification.

related_jiras.note: Published PA decision in the same AdministrativeGender family rejected adding an Intersex code and kept other, helping bound FHIR-14341 to the UN definition wording; it is already represented on the combined branch.
